samples.summary: New `['me','optional']` observer in CollabDocumentProvider defeats sheet-view's deliberate 5-minute staleTime
samples.evidence: `sheet-view.tsx:212-217` registers `useQuery({ queryKey: ['me','optional'], queryFn: fetchMeOptional, retry: false, staleTime: 5 * 60 * 1000 })`. `collab-document-provider.tsx:186-192` now registers a *second* observer on the same cache key with **no** `staleTime` (default 0). React Query resolves a shared query's staleness from the observers, so the entry is stale immediately and refetches on mount/focus — the 5-minute window the sheet view asks for no longer applies. `PublicRoute.tsx:11-15` reads the same key. Neither site was updated. The fix belongs on the new query in `collab-document-provider.tsx` (give it the same `staleTime`), not on sheet-view.

samples.summary: Every private editor route now fires a second `GET /auth/me`, for a feature that is dark at the pinned SDK version
samples.evidence: `['me','optional']` is a different cache key from the `['me']` entry `PrivateRoute.tsx:14` already resolved, so each of the six out-of-diff editor mounts — `docs-detail.tsx:351`, `slides-detail.tsx:952`, `document-detail.tsx:910`, `board-detail.tsx:261`, `notes-detail.tsx:378`, `files/pdf-collab.tsx:200` — now issues an extra identity request on open. `initialData` seeds the value but with default staleTime 0 the query still refetches on mount. `packages/frontend/package.json:66` pins `@yorkie-js/react` at `0.7.22`, below `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"`, so `supportsClientKey()` is false and no document can ever be durable on this build — the request buys nothing today.

samples.summary: OfflineRuntime is mounted unconditionally, adding a full document listing, an IndexedDB open and a cross-account sweep to every authenticated session even when persistence is impossible
samples.evidence: `PrivateRoute.tsx:35` renders `<OfflineRuntime userId=... />` with no capability or preference gate. `components/offline-runtime.tsx` then runs `retryPendingOfflineErase()`, constructs a `WafflebaseDocStore` (opening IndexedDB), calls `store.collectStale()` — which `lib/wafflebase-doc-store.ts` documents as deleting *every account's* entries older than 30 days — and issues `fetchDocuments()` (`api/documents.ts:35`, an unscoped `GET /documents`) on every session. With `@yorkie-js/react` pinned at `0.7.22` (`packages/frontend/package.json:66`) `supportsClientKey()` is false, so the store can never contain anything for this work to act on. Every other surface of the feature is behind `supportsClientKey()` (Settings section, chip offer, `useDurableDocument`); this one is not.

samples.summary: `deleteWorkspace` adds two unconditional requests before the DELETE, and bypasses the existing workspace-scoped document endpoint
samples.evidence: `workspaces.ts:127` calls `documentIdsIn(id)`, which at `workspaces.ts:103-104` issues `fetchWorkspace(ref)` and then `fetchDocuments()` — the *unscoped* listing of every document the user can read. `fetchWorkspaceDocuments(workspaceId)` already exists at `workspaces.ts:290` and is the scoped equivalent; it is not used. The only caller, `app/workspaces/workspace-settings.tsx:182`, previously made one request and now makes three, on every workspace deletion, regardless of whether anything was ever stored locally. `removeMember` (`workspaces.ts:160`) does the same when the leaving member is the signed-in user.

samples.summary: The shared PDF layout mounts CollabDocumentProvider outside `NonDurableScope`, so the share-link exclusion is not positional there
samples.evidence: `shared-document.tsx:1016` wraps the five CRDT share branches in `NonDurableScope`, but the PDF share layout at `shared-document.tsx:753-792` mounts its own `YorkieProvider` → `PdfCollabProvider` → `CollabDocumentProvider` (`app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:200`, `docKey={`pdf-${documentId}`}`) with no scope above it. It is non-durable today only because of the key-prefix exclusion `docKey.startsWith("pdf-")` at `lib/use-durable-document.ts:34` — the very rule the new code argues cannot express the share-link case. If PDFs ever gain a sync chip and that exclusion is relaxed, share-link PDF content becomes durable on the visitor's disk with nothing else refusing it. `src/app/shared/__tests__/shared-document-durability.test.tsx` only mocks the CRDT path, so nothing covers this branch.

samples.summary: `api/auth.ts` now statically imports the IndexedDB store, pulling the whole offline layer into the entry chunk for every user
samples.evidence: `api/auth.ts:4` adds `import { eraseOfflineDataOnLogout } from "@/lib/offline-erase"`, and `api/documents.ts:6` adds `purgeOfflineDocuments` from the same module. `lib/offline-erase.ts` statically imports `lib/wafflebase-doc-store.ts` (~1500 lines), `lib/durable-session.ts` and `lib/offline-persistence-preference.ts` — the last of which registers a module-scope `window.addEventListener('storage', ...)` (`offline-persistence-preference.ts` bottom). `api/auth.ts` is reached by essentially every route and by the eagerly-imported shell, so this code is now in the initial bundle and executed on load for all users, including the ones for whom `supportsClientKey()` is false. The recovery half was carefully kept behind `await import()` in `offline-runtime.tsx`; this half was not.
searchedFor: read api/auth.ts and api/documents.ts import blocks

finding.summary: Thirty-day sweep is cross-account but its open-document guard is scoped to one account, so it can purge another account's live entry in another tab
finding.evidence: `OfflineRuntime` builds the housekeeping store with `isOpenElsewhere: (docKey) => isOpenInAnyTab(docKey, { userId, whenUnknown: false })` (packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.tsx:75-81). `isOpenInAnyTab` narrows the lock-name prefix to `wb-durable:{thisUserId}:` (packages/frontend/src/lib/durable-session.ts, `prefix` computation in `isOpenInAnyTab`). But `WafflebaseDocStore.collectStale` deliberately enumerates aged headers for EVERY account on the device (`const aged = await this.headerKeysWhere(BY_UPDATED_AT, range)` — unscoped, and the doc-comment says "Live entries are collected **whoever wrote them**"). The two do not line up: a document held open by a DIFFERENT account in another tab holds `wb-durable:{otherUserId}:{docKey}`, which the user-scoped prefix filter never matches, so `isLive()` answers false and the entry is purged out from under that tab's live client. The `evicted` marker that would make the next append fail loudly is keyed per database in this tab's module memory (`evictedKeys` in wafflebase-doc-store.ts), so the other tab never sees it and its appends fall into the contract's silent "no base" success while its chip still reports the document saved. Reachability is limited by `load()` touching `updatedAt` on attach, so it needs a tab open longer than the max age — but the guard/scope mismatch is real and the fix belongs either on the sweep (scope it, or ask unscoped) or on `openElsewhere` (drop `userId` for the collector).

verdict.reason: The described defect is not present in this tree. OfflineRuntime supplies two liveness predicates, not one: the account-scoped `openElsewhere` (offline-runtime.tsx:76-77) and an explicitly unscoped `openAnywhere = (docKey) => isOpenInAnyTab(docKey, { whenUnknown: false })` (offline-runtime.tsx:86-87), both passed to the store as `isOpenElsewhere` and `isOpenForAnyUser` (offline-runtime.tsx:91-92). `isOpenInAnyTab` with no `userId` uses the unscoped prefix `"wb-durable:"` (durable-session.ts:383-386), so it matches any account's lock. `collectStale` does not call the scoped `isLive`; it calls `isLiveAnywhere` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1212), which prefers `isOpenForAnyUser` when supplied (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:432-440), with the option documented for precisely this cross-account hazard (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:138-154). Tests pin the behaviour: offline-runtime.test.tsx:171-173 exercises the unscoped predicate with another user's key, and wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts:598-602 asserts collectStale collects 0 when only `isOpenForAnyUser` reports the doc open. The reviewer's quoted evidence (sweep reaching the guard only via the user-scoped `isOpenElsewhere`) does not match the code.

finding.summary: Swallowing a failed `local-changes-dropped` subscription silently breaks the `expectLoss`-before-`remove` invariant the store relies on, turning an archive into an outright delete of unsent work
finding.evidence: `DurableLossWatch` is the ONLY production caller of `expectLoss` (`packages/frontend/src/components/durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:282`; grep for `expectLoss` finds no other non-test call site). `WafflebaseDocStore.remove()` reads that latch at `packages/frontend/src/lib/wafflebase-doc-store.ts:771` and only writes an archive when it is set (`if (record && losing)` at line 791), documented at lines 735-737 as "The latch is set from the `LocalChangesDropped` handler ... so the flag is always in place by the time the removal arrives." This delta wraps the subscription in `try { ... } catch { console.warn(...) }` for exactly the case the new comment cites — an SDK where `subscribe('local-changes-dropped')` throws `Unsupported event type`. On such an SDK the handler is never registered, yet the SDK still calls `store.remove()` on its three loss paths, so the removal takes the `losing === false` branch: snapshot, header and change log are deleted with no archive, `listRecoverableWork` has nothing to list, and the user's unreconciled edits are gone with only a console warning. Before this change the throw was loud (it crashed the subtree, so the document was not editable and nothing was silently deleted); after it, editing continues over a store whose loss path now deletes. Fix belongs on the new code: when the loss subscription specifically cannot be installed, the durable store must not be handed to the client as an archiving store (e.g. disable persistence / report undurable) rather than just warning. Confidence is medium only because node_modules is not installed here, so I could not confirm whether @yorkie-js/sdk 0.7.22 emits this event — but the diff's own justification asserts it may not.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts the refused `local-changes-dropped` subscription is swallowed with only a `console.warn`, leaving `expectLoss` uncalled so `remove()` deletes instead of archiving. The code is not as described. `watch()` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:295-306) returns a boolean, and the loss subscription's failure is explicitly compensated at lines 314-332: it latches the store conservatively via `durable.store.expectLoss?.(doc.getKey())` (line 325) so the next removal of that document archives, and it lowers the durability promise via `durable.reportUnreportable()` (line 331) — which is precisely the fix the finding prescribes. With the latch set, `remove()` reads `losing === true` at wafflebase-doc-store.ts:809 and takes the archiving branch at line 829, not the delete branch. The behaviour is directly covered by a test that makes `subscribe` throw `Unsupported event type` for `local-changes-dropped` and asserts both `not-durable` and `expectedLosses` containing the doc key (durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx:271-283). The finding's cited line numbers for the store (771/791) also do not match the actual read/branch (809/829). Ground: not-present.
